title: ALMA Band 1 observations of the ρ Oph W filament: I. Enhanced power from excess microwave emission at high spatial frequencies
question: Reveal the detailed morphology of the excess microwave emission (EME) signal in the rho Oph W filament free from imaging priors, constrain the spectral index of the high-frequency drop, and search for fine structure (PAH combs and CRRLs) in its spectrum.

data.angular_resolution: ~7 arcsec (natural-weight dirty beam 8.70'' x 6.44'' / -85.6 deg; effective model resolution ~1/3 of clean beam)
data.sensitivity: 1.53 uJy/beam (theoretical noise of natural-weights dirty map); 11 uJy/beam (CASA-tclean rms)

what.value: ATCA 17-39 GHz mosaics and 17.5 GHz and 20.2 GHz flux densities

evidence.quote: The ATCA images reported in (cite: Casassus2021MNRAS.502..589C) already fill in the missing spatial frequencies by incorporation of prior images in the synthesis imaging strategy.

what.value: Herschel Gould Belt Survey FIR images

evidence.loc: A compact EME source with no IR counterpart
evidence.quote: The point source has no FIR counterpart either (Fig. 8k-o), as shown by comparison with images from the Herschel Gould Belt Survey (cite: Herschel_2020A&A...638A..74L).
The IRAC images were obtained from the Set of Enhanced Imaging Products (SEIP), which is part of the Spitzer Heritage Archive.

recipe.goal: Fit and subtract bright point sources in the uv-plane
recipe.method: Bin visibilities into 60-channel bins with CASA mstransform; fit positions, flux densities at 40.15 GHz, and spectral indices for SR 4, ISO-Oph-17, and DoAr 21 in each execution block separately using pyralysis and iminuit; subtract point-source models from unaveraged visibilities and verify by extracting channel-by-channel point-source spectra.
key_parameters: reference frequency nu_0 = 40.15 GHz; 60-channel bins; 4 nearest fields used for DoAr 21, closest field for SR 4 and ISO-Oph-17
assumptions: Airy disk approximation to the ALMA primary beam

recipe.method: Fit a 1024x1024 pixel model image directly to non-gridded visibilities across the 16 fields using gpu-uvmem; restore by adding the Gaussian-smoothed model image to the natural-weighted linear mosaic of residual dirty maps; compare against multi-scale CASA-tclean image.
key_parameters: N = 1024^2 pixels of 1''x1'', sigma_I = 100 uJy/beam pre-conditioning, lambda = 0 (truncated at 10 iterations) and lambda = 0.1; tclean: mtmfs, nterms=1, robust=2, scales=[0,15,38,70], gain=0.05
assumptions: Flat spectral index in flux density (alpha = 0) when propagating model image across frequencies; Airy-disk primary beam

recipe.goal: Place upper limits on Carbon Radio Recombination Lines (CRRLs)
recipe.method: Stack the four CRRLs (C56alpha to C53alpha) within the correlator setup in a joint imaging.
assumptions: Turbulent linewidths ~2 km/s; LTE conditions and negligible depopulation factors above 100 K for comparison

recipe.goal: Extract intra-band diffuse emission spectrum and spectral index
recipe.method: Simulate visibilities on the pure-chi2 deconvolved model image template I^m using pyralysis, perform weighted linear regression in the uv-plane at each frequency channel (or 120-channel bin) to get slope a_nu, and fit a power law in frequency.
key_parameters: 120-channel average (16 channels); reference frequency nu_0 = 36.63 GHz; pure-chi2 template (lambda = 0)
assumptions: Template image I^m has flat spectral index across the band

recipe.goal: Cross-correlate ALMA Band 1 visibilities with Spitzer-IRAC templates
recipe.method: Remove stellar point sources from IRAC maps using StarXTerminator in PixInsight; simulate Band 1 visibilities on star-subtracted IRAC maps with pyralysis; compute linear regression slopes a_IR and complex visibility Pearson r coefficients across all baselines and as a function of uv-radius bins.
assumptions: Coarser angular resolution of IRAC 8.0 um (1.98'') vs ALMA (~7'') introduces negligible bias

recipe.goal: Estimate interferometric flux loss and extract multi-frequency SEDs
recipe.method: Integrate product of images and linear mosaic attenuation map A(x) over selected field apertures for ALMA Band 1, ATCA, IRAC, and Herschel maps; estimate Band 1 flux-loss factor f_B1 by comparing input vs gpu-uvmem restored flux density on simulated IRAC 3.6 um visibilities.
key_parameters: Fixed 10% error on radio flux densities; apertures defined by field subsets (all, 5-6, 7-10, 6, 7-9)
assumptions: Band 1 signal follows the same large-scale power spectrum as the IRAC 3.6 um template for flux-loss estimation

recipe.goal: Search for and place limits on PAH rotational frequency combs
recipe.method: Rectify the cross-correlation spectrum a_nu by dividing by the power-law fit and subtracting the weighted mean; project onto a basis of comb functions with line spacing Delta_nu_line using a matched-filter dot product across all 4 spectral windows.
key_parameters: S = 4 spectral windows, C = 1920 channels each; scan Delta_nu_line from twice the frequency resolution up to 200 MHz, sampling every tenth of a resolution element (~2000 values); tested native resolution and 5-channel bins
assumptions: Imperfect planar PAHs with D6h or D3h quasi-symmetry and permanent dipole arising from defects produce regularly spaced frequency combs

score_reason: The calibration versions, flagging, equations for visibility-plane point-source fitting, cross-correlation, and comb matched-filtering are explicitly written out, and imaging parameters for both gpu-uvmem and CASA-tclean are well documented. Reproduction is slightly hindered by reliance on proprietary AI star-removal software (PixInsight/StarXTerminator) for the IRAC templates and unstated fitted coordinates for the subtracted point sources.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA dataset (2023.1.00265.S) is standard pipeline-calibrated data, the mathematical equations for uv-plane point-source fitting, template cross-correlation, and comb filtering are fully specified in the text, and the main results (point-source fluxes/spectral indices, diffuse EME spectral indices, CRRL upper limit) are concrete numeric targets.
